title: Goalpost: A Certification-Gated Protocol for Auditing the Stability of LLM Screening Decisions, Reasons, and Recourse
description:
Release status: v1.0.2 is the current correction release and supersedes the preserved v1.0.1 historical archive.

Goalpost is an open instrument for auditing decision, reason and recourse stability in LLM-mediated screening configurations — any configuration its operator controls. It measures one property, repeat-consistency: run the same case through the same system repeatedly and check whether the decision, the reasons given, and the advice (what the candidate should change) come back the same. Not accuracy, not fairness — those are different measurements, deliberately out of scope.

Structured outputs are parsed deterministically and have no extraction reader in the measurement path. For free-text outputs, a pre-registered certification gate requires the extraction reader's measured self-agreement a to clear 0.90 and either the observed stability s to be at least 0.85 or a to exceed s by at least 0.15. Extraction noise preferentially manufactures instability but can also inflate overlap; the asymmetry is a conservative design choice, not an identity. Where the gate fails, the result is published as withheld.

This archive contains the instrument; audits across published screening tools and lab configurations; pre-registrations with amendment logs; run-level transcripts, normalised sets, metrics, reports and metered costs; and an append-only decision log. Some pipeline stages and retries are outside the instrument's meter, so provider dashboards are the cost source of truth for those calls. One unlicensed upstream's prompts are fetched from a pinned, hash-verified commit and are not redistributed.
